explain.say: Here is a puzzle for you: when did the Middle Ages end? A Greek scholar might say 1453, a Spanish sailor 1492, a German theologian 1517. Periodisation means dividing time into named eras, and every division is an argument. Look at the timeline of candidate dates.

explain.say: Look at the second dot. In the 1340s the Italian poet Petrarch called the centuries after Rome an age of darkness, because he admired ancient Latin. That is where the idea of Dark Ages began. By the 1680s the German scholar Christoph Cellarius had fixed ancient, medieval and modern in textbooks. Was the medieval world really dark?

explain.say: Now the dates for the end: 1453, when Constantinople fell to the Ottomans; 1492, Columbus; or 1517, Luther. Each one assumes a different thing mattered most. The French historian Jacques Le Goff even argued for a long Middle Ages lasting into the eighteenth century. Which end date would you choose, and why?

explain.say: Periodisation travels badly. Look at the comparison. In 1817 James Mill split Indian history into Hindu, Muslim and British periods, labels by religion that suggested permanent divides. Many historians now prefer ancient, early medieval, medieval and early modern or colonial. Why might Mill's labels still matter in politics today?

Other societies count time differently: Chinese history by dynasties, the Islamic calendar from the Hijra in 622, and geologists now debate an Anthropocene, a new age shaped by humans. Excellent thinking. Exam tip: when you use a period label, add one sentence on who made it and what it assumes.

faq.q: Who invented the idea of the Middle Ages?
faq.a: Italian humanists from Petrarch in the 1340s saw a dark time between ancient Rome and their own revival. Later scholars, notably Christoph Cellarius in the 1680s, made the three-part scheme of ancient, medieval and modern standard.
asks: Where does the term Dark Ages come from?

faq.q: When did the Middle Ages end?
faq.a: There is no single answer. Common choices are 1453, the fall of Constantinople, 1492, Columbus's voyage, or 1517, the start of the Reformation; some historians, like Jacques Le Goff, argue for a much later end.
asks: What year did the medieval period end?

faq.a: Because names and boundaries carry judgments: dark versus renaissance, or periods named by religion or by colonial rule. They shape what seems important and who seems to belong.
asks: Why do historians argue about periods?

faq.q: What was wrong with James Mill's periods of Indian history?
faq.a: His 1817 scheme of Hindu, Muslim and British periods defined eras by the religion of rulers, implied a golden age and decline, and fed later communal politics. Most historians now use other labels.
asks: Why do historians criticise James Mill?

faq.a: A label for roughly 1450 to 1800, between the medieval and modern periods, used for Europe and increasingly for the world. It suggests these centuries pointed towards modernity, which some historians question.
asks: What years are the early modern period?

facts: Romulus Augustulus, the last emperor in the West, was deposed in 476.
James Mill's The History of British India was published in 1817.
The Islamic calendar counts from the Hijra in 622 CE.
